subject: HoloHealth pricing — seat bundles vs runtime credits
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@holohealth.com>
Cc: procurement@holohealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: HoloHealth pricing — seat bundles vs runtime credits

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — good to see the latency numbers holding up on your sample prompts. Attached is an updated commercial outline that walks through two packaging approaches we discussed: (A) seat-based bundle (predictable seats + modest overage credits) and (B) runtime-credit model (consumption-first, per-token). The file is: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (proposal summary + sample billing scenarios).

Quick notes:
- Seat bundle is simpler for your product team to budget (fixed per-month cost, academic pricing tiers available).
- Runtime credits give you flexibility for bursty inference and can reduce unit cost on very spiky workloads but requires a slightly higher ops integration (token accounting, pre-batching).

Before I put together a formal counter that tries to bridge with the AtlasAI quote you mentioned, can you confirm:
1) your expected 90th percentile daily tokens over the pilot (ballpark)?
2) are you evaluating a hosted flow (our Redwood API) or dedicated capacity?

If you can share the competitor quote, I’ll run a short economic comparison and propose a limited-time pilot credit + a packaging concession so we stay competitive and protect revenue.

Thanks — I’ve penciled a short call Fri 11am PT if you want to walk the scenarios.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachment: redwood-proposal-v2.pdf (PDF, 42KB)
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@holohealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@holohealth.com
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HoloHealth pricing — seat bundles vs runtime credits

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the options.

Quick answers:
- 90th percentile daily tokens for the pilot: ~18M tokens/day (spiky, mainly batch inference during overnight processing).
- We're planning to start on hosted (API) for the pilot and then evaluate dedicated in Q4 if performance & cost meet expectations.

I've attached the competing quote from AtlasAI (atlasai-quote.pdf). Key ask from procurement: can Redwood match effective cost per inference once you normalize for model variant and batching? Atlas is offering an upfront credit + ~30% off listed runtime pricing for the first 6 months.

Also, procurement would like clarity on whether pilot credits can be applied to both hosted and dedicated transitions (we may want to reserve credits toward a dedicated commitment).

If you can send a side-by-side that shows seat-bundle vs runtime-credit economics for our token profile (18M 90th percentile), that would help us finalize an internal recommendation.

Samir
Head of Platform | HoloHealth
samir.khan@holohealth.com

Attachment: atlasai-quote.pdf (PDF, 28KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: HoloHealth pricing — seat bundles vs runtime credits

Stephanie, Irene — looping you both in with a recommended commercial play.

Notes after quick econ run (assumes Atlas discount and their quoted throughput):
- Offer option 1 (mix): 15% off standard seat bundle for first 3 months, then 10% for months 4–6. + $20k pilot credit applied to hosted usage.
- Offer option 2 (aggressive parity): 20% off seat bundle for 6 months + $35k pilot credit but requires a 12-month minimum and a 60-day notice if they downgrade.

Rationale: seat bundle preserves revenue visibility, reduces billing friction for their product team, and gives us an easier lift to stay competitive. The higher credit in option 2 can be justified for strategic logos, but we need approvals on contract length and downgrade penalties.

Irene — can you confirm whether pilot credits are transferable to a dedicated commitment or if we need to document a conversion clause (credits applied as first X months of dedicated spend)? Also flag any security/contract asks we should pre-authorize.

Stephanie — if you think HoloHealth is strategic, push option 2; otherwise start with option 1 and keep room to step up. Happy to join the call Fri.

-Jordan
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Aug 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: HoloHealth pricing — seat bundles vs runtime credits

Quick legal/security check:
- Pilot credits: we can make them convertible to dedicated spend, but must be explicit in the SOW/Order Form (i.e., credits will apply as a dollar-for-dollar credit against the first 3 invoices on the dedicated contract).
- Data residency: HoloHealth's PHI workflows require confirmation that logs are retained only in US regions for hosted pilots. I recommend we include the SOC2 snapshot and the standard data residency clause. Attached soc2-snapshot.pdf for their security team.
- Contract caveat: if we offer the 20% for 6 months + $35k, request a 12-month minimum and a 30% acceleration clause if they terminate early (protects revenue).

I'll draft the minimal SOW language if you want me to.

Irene Choi
Head of Legal & Security | Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

Attachment: soc2-snapshot.pdf (PDF, 12KB)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@holohealth.com>
Cc: procurement@holohealth.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HoloHealth pricing — seat bundles vs runtime credits

Samir — thanks for the quick turnaround and the Atlas quote. Based on our internal alignment, here’s a concise counter that balances HoloHealth’s budget ask and Redwood’s commercial guardrails.

Counteroffer (two paths):

1) Pragmatic starter (lower commitment)
- 15% off standard seat bundle for months 1–3, 10% for months 4–6
- $20,000 pilot credit applied to hosted usage (applies to pilot invoices only)
- No long-term commitment required; standard MSAs apply

2) Strategic conversion (recommended if HoloHealth wants price stability)
- 20% off seat bundle for the first 6 months
- $35,000 pilot credit which is convertible to dedicated spend (applies as credit against first 3 invoices on a dedicated contract)
- 12-month minimum commitment with a 30% acceleration clause on early termination

Security & SOW points
- Pilot will run in US region only; we’ll provide SOC2 snapshot and a short addendum that enumerates log retention limits.
- Irene will draft the SOW language around conversion of credits into dedicated spend.

Next steps
- If you want the strategic package, I can get legal to prepare a one-page addendum and a DocuSign for signatures (link below). If you prefer the starter pack, we can get the pilot kicked off immediately after PO.

DocuSign link (strategic package): https://www.docusign.com/txn/ABC12345
Redwood counter (PDF): redwood-counter-holohealth.pdf

Can we lock a 30-minute slot Mon 8/16 at 10am PT to finalize?

Thanks — excited to get HoloHealth onto the platform.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
